summary: At just 0.6 square miles, Contra Costa Centre is less a traditional city and more a purpose-built cluster of mid-rise offices, transit-oriented housing, and retail wrapped tightly around a BART station — one of the densest pockets in the East Bay at nearly 12,000 people per square mile. That BART access is the defining infrastructure fact: it puts downtown San Francisco roughly 35 minutes away without touching a freeway, which helps explain why a median household income of nearly $128,000 coexists with a median home value around $724,500 — a price-to-income ratio of about 5.7, steep but noticeably less punishing than much of the inner Bay Area. The landscape sits in the broad, sun-warmed corridor between the East Bay hills and Mount Diablo, averaging 9.4 hours of sunshine daily with highs around 70°F — warmer and drier than San Francisco by a wide margin. The tradeoff is tangible: the area is compact and walkable within its footprint but hemmed in by Interstate 680 and large commercial parcels, so the transition from urban density to freeway infrastructure can feel abrupt within a few blocks. Median rent north of $2,600 reflects that transit proximity commands a premium even when the surrounding terrain is more office park than charming main street — a place where the commute math works better than the sense of place.
